meta.title: Operation of Digital Rota Rod Apparatus in Pharmacology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To assess motor coordination, balance, and muscle relaxant effects of CNS-active drugs in rodents by measuring the ability of animals to remain on a rotating rod.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for screening muscle relaxant activity, sedative-hypnotic toxicity (motor incoordination), and neurological drug effects in mice and rats.
procedure: Switch on the digital rota rod apparatus; allow the motor to warm up for 2–3 minutes.
Set the rotation speed using the digital control panel: typically 10–25 RPM for mice; 5–15 RPM for rats.
Select operating mode: fixed speed (constant rotation); accelerating mode (gradual increase from low to high RPM over set time).
Set the cut-off time to prevent injury to animals (typically 180 seconds maximum).
Pre-train animals on the rota rod for 3 consecutive days before the experiment — select animals that can remain on the rod for ≥ 180 seconds.
On experiment day: record the pre-drug baseline performance (fall-off time) for each animal.
Administer the test drug or vehicle by the specified route.
Test animals at the specified time points post-administration (e.g., 30, 60, 90 minutes).
Place the animal on the rotating rod — the automatic fall sensor starts the timer when the animal is placed, stops when it falls.
Record the fall-off time (time until the animal falls or makes 3 complete passive rotations).
Return the animal to its cage after each test; test again at the next time point.
Disinfect the rod section between animals with 70% ethanol and allow to dry.
Calculate mean fall-off time for each group; compare drug vs. control using statistical analysis.
Record all data in the experimental record sheet.
precautions: Do not force animals to stay on the rod — they must fall naturally for the test to be valid.
Ensure the fall-detection platform/photobeam is correctly set to detect animal falls.
Place a soft cushion below the apparatus to protect animals from fall-related injury.
Pre-train animals adequately — untrained animals do not show reliable baseline performance, making drug effects undetectable.
Clean the rod between animals — odour from a previous animal causes the next animal stress.
Set a humane cut-off time (180 seconds) — do not allow animals to attempt continuously without rest.
Follow CPCSEA and IAEC guidelines for care and use of laboratory animals.
